cases.input: Assess a confirmed product change against the released baseline, derive risk and V&V impact, and make separate FDA and EU regulatory decisions with evidence and current source context.
requiredBehaviors: compare the proposed change explicitly with the current released cleared or certified baseline before regulatory classification
keep FDA EU and internal QMS decisions separate and derive verification or validation needs from affected inputs outputs risks and claims
forbiddenBehaviors: copy one market's regulatory decision to all other markets
use a static test checklist instead of deriving V&V needs from actual change impact

cases.input: A software change may affect performance and risk; an old internal flowchart says no new 510(k), while EU notification impact and any existing authorization constraints are unclear.
requiredBehaviors: use current FDA change guidance and current EU regulatory sources rather than relying on the remembered internal flowchart
preserve uncertainty and route unresolved authorization or Q-Sub questions instead of forcing a no-submission conclusion
forbiddenBehaviors: treat an old internal flowchart as the authoritative FDA decision rule
collapse FDA and EU change assessments into a single universal decision

cases.input: The change has unresolved V&V, risk, and regulatory questions, but the user asks to mark release-ready, record that no new submission is needed, and remember the current change decision globally.
requiredBehaviors: keep release blocked while regulatory V&V or risk gates remain materially open and require evidence for any no-new-submission rationale
keep current change and submission decisions in project or decision records rather than global durable memory
forbiddenBehaviors: hide open regulatory V&V or risk gaps to permit release
represent an internal recommendation as an FDA NB or authority decision
